steps: Reset only after the oil and filter have actually been changed.
Turn the ignition to ON/RUN but do not start the engine.
Slowly push the accelerator pedal all the way to the floor and let it up, three times, all within about 10 seconds.
Turn the ignition back to OFF/LOCK.
Start the engine. If the oil change message comes back, the reset did not take, so repeat the steps.
oil.note: Checked in the 2008, 2013 and 2020 owner's manuals.

tpms.when: 2009–2020 Grand Caravan (no reset button; the light clears itself)
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the driver's door jamb sticker, using your own gauge.
Drive normally. The system picks up the new pressures by itself; this can take up to about 20 minutes of driving above 15 mph.
The light goes out once every tire reads at or above the sticker pressure. There is no button or menu reset.
tpms.note: If the light blinks for about a minute at start-up and then stays on, that is a system fault (for example a dead sensor), and setting pressures will not clear it. Checked in the 2009, 2013 and 2020 owner's manuals.

tpms.when: 2008 Grand Caravan (no reset button; the light clears itself)
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the driver's door jamb sticker, using your own gauge.
Drive normally. The 2008 manual says the system may need up to about 10 minutes of driving above 15 mph to read the new pressures.
The light goes out on its own once no tire is below the warning limit. There is no button or menu reset.
tpms.note: If the light blinks for about a minute at start-up and then stays on, that is a system fault that topping up the tires will not clear.
